newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean bond yields end lower on gov't steps news.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean bond yields end lower on gov't steps news.

text.p: Key bond yields closed sharply lower on Wednesday on active buying boosted by news that the government was strongly committed to lowering money market rates, dealers said.
Yields on both three-year corproate bonds and three-month CDs each closed 30 basis points lower.
"New issuances were ample today, but the news that the government planned to lower money market rates triggered active buying by most institutions," said Hyundai Securities dealer Kang Yung-gee.
On Wednesday, an official at the ruling New Korea Party said the party had agreed with the government to lower money market rates by one to two percent to help the corporate sector.
No date has yet been set for the rate cut, however.
The overnight call rate remained unchanged as cash demand and supply continued to be well matched, dealers said.
They predicted the benchmark three-year yields were likely to fall further on Thursday as the hopes for falling interest rates would continue to boost the buying sentiment.
